study.setting: One high school in Turkey; grades 9-11
study.outcome: Closed-book, closed-laptop exam immediately after practice within each session; all three groups tested without AI.

arms.label: No AI
arms.practice: Textbooks and notes; no provided device

arms.label: GPT Base
arms.practice: GPT-4 chat interface with basic tutoring prompt

arms.label: GPT Tutor
arms.practice: GPT-4 with teacher-provided solutions and hints plus instructions not to give full answers

study.excluded: Honors-designated classrooms excluded from the main specification
study.estimand: Intention-to-treat difference from the no-AI control
study.standard_errors: HC1 robust standard errors clustered by classroom

published_table_1.outcome_scale: Authors' normalized exam grade from 0 to 1
published_table_1.unit: Score points on the authors' 0-1 scale

rows.label: No AI
rows.role: Omitted reference category; zero is a contrast baseline, not its exam score

rows.label: GPT Base
rows.p_value_statement: P < 0.05 as reported; exact p-value not given in Table 1

rows.label: GPT Tutor
rows.p_value_statement: Not statistically significant; exact p-value not given in Table 1

published_table_1.published_confidence_interval_note: Table 1 reports standard errors, not CI endpoints.

practice_context.note: Practice was assisted in the treatment arms. Do not mix these outcomes with the unaided-exam chart.

interpretation.headline: GPT Base reduced unaided exam scores by about 17% relative to the control mean; GPT Tutor showed no detectable difference.
interpretation.denominator: Published no-AI control-arm mean exam score, 0.321
interpretation.conversion: Multiply the published 0-1 coefficient by 100: -0.054 -> -5.4 points on a 0-100 score scale, equivalently -5.4 percentage points of maximum score.
interpretation.tutor_null: Statistically indistinguishable from no AI; does not establish equivalence or an exactly zero effect.
interpretation.avoid: Do not call the result a 17-percentage-point fall; do not claim the tutor improves unaided performance; do not replace its -0.004 estimate with zero.

chart.title: Effect of practice support on subsequent unaided exam scores
chart.subtitle: Adjusted difference from no-AI control
chart.transformation: Published coefficient and standard error multiplied by 100. No control=100 rebasing.

error_bars.limitations: Computed from rounded table entries. They do not use a finite-cluster t critical value and are not published CI endpoints.
error_bars.caption_required: Points are published adjusted estimates; bars are approximate 95% intervals calculated from published clustered standard errors.
error_bars.alternative: Omit derived intervals and display the published SEs in the data table if the renderer cannot distinguish calculated from published uncertainty.

chart.caption: Bastani et al., PNAS 2025, Table 1. All groups took the exam without AI. Main model: 2,848 student-session observations.
chart.reference_note: No AI at zero denotes the reference for treatment effects, not an observed score of zero.

optional_raw_group_means.purpose: A defensible alternative three-group score chart, explicitly unadjusted; does not reproduce the adjusted 17% result.
optional_raw_group_means.extraction: Parse CSV with headers exactly as provided. Filter Honors == 0. Group by GPTBase/GPTTutor indicators. Take arithmetic mean of Part3Tot across nonmissing student-session rows.
optional_raw_group_means.weighting: Each available student-session has equal weight; students attending more sessions contribute more rows.
optional_raw_group_means.unit: Mean exam score on authors' 0-1 scale
optional_raw_group_means.note: Means computed from public data, not treatment-group means printed in Table 1. SD is not SE. No naive independent-observation confidence intervals: repeated students and classroom assignment matter. Regression excludes incomplete covariate rows; raw means include all 2,899 non-honors student-sessions.

limitations: Short-term unaided performance after classroom practice; no direct long-term skill-decay estimate.
One Turkish high school and mathematics tasks; broader population and workplace generalization are untested here.
The tutor intervention bundled teacher-designed guidance and correct solutions with guardrails; the experiment does not isolate each component.
A nonsignificant tutor coefficient is not evidence of statistical equivalence.
Raw group differences differ from covariate-adjusted intention-to-treat coefficients.

human_review_flags.check: Check Table 1 column (2): Base -0.054 (SE 0.022), Tutor -0.004 (SE 0.013), control mean 0.321.
Confirm 17% is relative to 0.321; the absolute difference is 5.4 points out of 100, not 17 percentage points.
Show Tutor's nonzero estimate and uncertainty; do not call it proven equivalent to control.
If error bars are plotted, label them derived approximate 95% intervals, not published CIs.
Keep the coefficient chart separate from raw group means; do not place a 17% annotation on the unadjusted means.
Label 2,848 as student-session observations; all three groups completed the exam unaided. Human sign-off remains outstanding.
